input: Set a monthly charitable giving goal

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The monthly dollar amount or percentage of income they can realistically commit to is the single most foundational number in this plan — everything else scales around it.
Whether they want to give to one specific cause, several causes, or are still exploring entirely shapes how the goal is structured and researched.
If this is a personal goal, a household/family decision, or tied to a business, the decision-making process, buy-in needed, and total budget all change.
What 'done well' looks like differs greatly — maximising impact per dollar, emotional fulfillment, community connection, or tax efficiency all point to different strategies.
Whether they want to automate recurring donations, give manually each month, or use a donor-advised fund determines the tools and systems needed.
Whether they are starting from scratch or already give sporadically changes whether the task is about building new habits or formalising existing ones.
Some people prefer giving to large vetted organisations, others to local grassroots efforts — this preference steers which charities are even considered.

gold.taskTitle: Set a monthly charitable giving goal
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to establish a clear, actionable monthly charitable giving goal, which may involve choosing a target amount, selecting causes or organizations, and building a system to track and follow through.

questions.title: What monthly budget can you realistically commit to giving?
questions.description: Identify the financial constraint — whether expressed as a fixed dollar amount, a percentage of income, or a range — that anchors the entire goal.

questions.title: Which cause areas do you most want to support?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has specific causes in mind (e.g., education, climate, poverty) or needs help exploring and narrowing down options.

questions.title: Is this a personal goal or a shared household decision?
questions.description: Clarify who is involved in setting and committing to the goal, as this affects the planning process, accountability, and total budget.

questions.title: What does a successful giving goal look like to you?
questions.description: Understand the user's primary measure of success — whether that is maximising measurable impact, supporting causes they feel connected to, achieving tax benefits, or building a consistent habit.

questions.title: Do you prefer automated recurring donations or manual monthly giving?
questions.description: Determine the preferred logistics and tools — auto-debits, donor-advised funds, or intentional monthly manual transfers — to design a system that fits their habits.

questions.title: Are you starting fresh or formalising giving you already do?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is building a brand-new habit from zero or trying to bring structure and intentionality to existing sporadic donations.

questions.title: Do you prefer large established charities or local grassroots organisations?
questions.description: Capture the user's style preference for the type of organisation they want to support, which directly narrows the list of candidates to research.
